paras: Good evening, Mr. de Souza. Here is Thursday, so you have it before you sleep.
MORNING. The car is at the hotel door at seven thirty in the morning, not at eight. Breakfast is from seven, so you have half an hour. The driver's name is Paul.
The first meeting is at nine, in the old building on Market Street, and it finishes at eleven. After that you are free until lunch.
AFTERNOON. Lunch is at one, and it is a long one, maybe two hours. In the afternoon there is nothing until five. At five thirty there is a short visit, twenty minutes, ten minutes from the hotel.
EVENING. Dinner is at eight, at the Blue Door, and we are nine people. Please be early, because the restaurant is small and they close the kitchen at ten thirty.
One change from yesterday: the meeting on Friday is now in the morning, not in the afternoon. Friday morning, at ten.

listenings.text: Hi, it's Paul, your driver. I am calling about tomorrow, because there are two changes and I do not want you to wait in the street. First, I come at seven thirty in the morning, not at eight. I know we said eight, but the traffic on Thursday is very bad after eight, so we need the extra half hour. Second, in the afternoon I cannot come at five, because I have another car at that time. My colleague comes instead, and his name is Tomas. Same car, different driver. Everything else is the same: dinner at eight, and I take you back to the hotel after that. If seven thirty is too early, call me tonight, not tomorrow morning. Thank you, and good night.

People ask me how I do it, so here is my day, and it is not complicated. I get up at five thirty, every day, and I do not use an alarm any more. From six to seven I walk, always, and that is the only hour of the day that is only mine. I have breakfast at seven with my children, and after that the day belongs to other people. I start work at eight thirty and I stop at six, and I do not answer the phone after eight in the evening. On Saturday I work in the morning, but never in the afternoon. On Sunday I do nothing, and that is not laziness, it is the reason the other six days work. I go to bed at ten. That is it. No secret.

extra_audio.text: Good morning. What time is the car tomorrow? At seven thirty, not at eight? And the meeting is at nine, is that right? I finish at eleven. See you in the morning.
